Colombia assets (not in balance sheet above): Home ≈ $375K (1.2B COP at 3,200 COP/USD) + bank accounts ≈ $9K (30M COP). These are illiquid or abroad; the combined net worth including them is approximately $942K. The investment plan focuses on building income-generating COP assets (CDTs, TES bonds) rather than relying on home equity.

Income and Spending

Cash flow note: Monthly income ($7,488) falls $827 short of recurring spending ($8,315). The $5,200/month invested via Wealthfront is drawn from the $310K liquid reserve — it is relocation of assets, not a cash surplus. The reserve provides 37+ months of runway at current burn and 50+ months without the investment contributions.

Asset Allocation

The portfolio is currently concentrated in cash and a short bond ladder. Full deployment to the 7-class target requires a phased transition over 2–3 months (see Investment Plan for details).

Currency Exposure

The 80/20 USD/COP target is set to hedge currency risk while keeping the bulk of the portfolio in the more liquid USD market. Closing the 17.4pp COP gap requires approximately $62K in new COP-denominated income-generating investments (CDTs, TES bonds).

5-Year Net Worth Projection

Based on $557,994 starting net worth, –$827/month net cash flow (income minus recurring spending), and no additional one-time expenditures. Returns applied to the full investable base.

Projected Net Worth by Scenario
Scenario Year 1 Year 3 Year 5
Base Case (7.5%) $589,920 $661,133 $743,430
Conservative (5%) $575,970 $614,662 $657,321
Optimistic (9%) $598,289 $690,087 $799,151

All three scenarios comfortably exceed the $500K estate goal through Year 5 — growth is driven by investment returns on the existing $558K asset base, not by new cash contributions.
